problems.title: Maximum distance between two centred circles
problems.question: A=(3cosα,3sinα), B=(4cosβ,4sinβ), withα∈[0,199],β∈[0,19.9]. MaximiseAB.
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: Both points lie on circles centred at the origin, so AB≤3+4=7.
steps: The bound is attained byα=π,β=0, which lie in the stated radian intervals and give opposite points.

problems.title: Equal values at supplementary arguments
problems.question: Which listed function agrees at 11π/5,−6π/5,4π/5?
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: Reduce modulo2π:the arguments becomeπ/5,4π/5,4π/5.
steps: Since sin(π−t)=sint, the sine values are all equal. Directly checking the other listed functions gives a different first value.

problems.title: Remove absolute values in the fourth quadrant
problems.question: Evaluate sinα|sinα|+cosα|cosα| for 3π/2<α<2π.
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: In quadrant IV, sinα<0, cosα>0.
steps: The expression is −sin²α+cos²α=cos2α.

problems.title: Recover lengths from their difference of squares
problems.question: Two inclined segments from one point to a plane differ by 7; their projections are 15,6. Find the point-to-plane distance.
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: If inclined lengths are L>s, then L²−s²=15²−6²=189.
steps: SinceL−s=7, we get L+s=27, so L=17, s=10.
The common height is √(10²−6²)=8.

problems.title: Signed heights obey the parallelogram identity
problems.question: A parallelogram lies entirely on one side of a plane. Vertex distances are AA₁=1, BB₁=2, CC₁=3. FindDD₁.
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: An affine signed height satisfiesh_A+h_C=h_B+h_D. All heights have the same sign here.
steps: Thus1+3=2+h_D, givingh_D=2.

problems.title: Recognise the tangent addition law
problems.question: Which listed function satisfiesf(x+y)=[f(x)+f(y)]/[1−f(x)f(y)]?
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: $\tan(x+y)=\frac{\tan x+\tan y}{1-\tan x\tan y}$.
steps: The tangent function satisfies the identity wherever all displayed terms are defined.

problems.title: Compare sine,angle and tangent
problems.question: Ordera=sin(π/6), b=π/6, c=tan(π/6).
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
steps: Thereforea<b<c.

problems.title: Triple-angle identities
problems.question: Simplify(4sin³x−3sinx)/(4cos³x−3cosx).
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: Numerator=−sin3x; denominator=cos3x.
steps: The quotient is −tan3x, withcos3x≠0 as required by the original fraction.

problems.title: A point equidistant from three triangle vertices
problems.question: A triangle has sides √10,√6,4. A spatial point K is 3 from every vertex. Find its distance to the triangle plane.
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: Because10+6=16, the triangle is right and its circumradius is 4/2=2. K projects to the circumcentre.
steps: The right triangle of common distance 3, circumradius2, and plane distanceh givesh²=9−4=5.

problems.title: Project two perpendicular spatial directions
problems.question: AB=2 is parallel to a plane at distance 2. BC⊥AB meets the plane at 30°. Find the plane projection length of AC.
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: The projection of BC has length 2cot30°=2√3. It remains perpendicular to the projected AB.
steps: The projected AC is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs2,2√3. Its length is √(4+12)=4.

problems.title: Find an angle sum through tangent
problems.question: Acute anglesx, y satisfysinx=1/√5, siny=1/√10. Findx+y.
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: Positive cosines give tanx=1/2, tany=1/3.
steps: The tangent addition formula gives tan(x+y)=(1/2+1/3)/(1−1/6)=1.
Also0<x+y<π, so the only angle with positive tangent1 there is π/4.

problems.title: Double-angle values from a tangent
problems.question: Evaluate[sin(2α)+tan(2α)]/[cos(2α)−tan(2α)] iftanα=2.
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: sin2α=2tanα/(1+tan²α)=4/5; cos2α=(1−tan²α)/(1+tan²α)=−3/5; tan2α=−4/3.
steps: The numerator is 4/5−4/3=−8/15; the denominator is −3/5+4/3=11/15.
Their quotient is −8/11.

problems.title: A sixth-power sum in terms of a sine-cosine sum
problems.question: Ifsinα+cosα=k, find 4(sin⁶α+cos⁶α).
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: Letu=sin²α, v=cos²α. Thenu+v=1, uv=[(k²−1)/2]², andu³+v³=1−3uv.
steps: Multiply by 4 to obtain4−3(k²−1)²=−3k⁴+6k²+1.

problems.title: A plane’s inclinations to perpendicular diagonals
problems.question: A plane through one rhombus side makes30°,60° with its diagonals. Find cosine of the rhombus acute angle.
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: Take perpendicular diagonal unit directionsu, v. A unit plane normal has component magnitudes sin30°=1/2, sin60°=√3/2 along them.
steps: Their squared sum is 1, so the normal lies in the rhombus plane. A side direction is proportional topu+qv, where p, q are diagonal lengths; normal orthogonality givesp:q=√3:1 or 1:√3.
For a rhombus, the cosine of its acute angle is|p²−q²|/(p²+q²)=(3−1)/(3+1)=1/2.

problems.title: Angle between two hypotenuse directions
problems.question: Right triangles ABK, ABP share leg AB=1 and for m a 45° dihedral angle; their hypotenuses are 3,√2. Find the smaller angle between them.
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: Other legs are BK=√(9−1)=2√2, BP=√(2−1)=1. Their directions make45°.
steps: VectorsAK, AP have common AB component1. Their dot product is 1+BK·BP·cos45°=3.
The product of their lengths is 3√2, so the cosine is 1/√2 and the angle 45°.

problems.title: A scaled sine’s least period
problems.question: For how many realais the least positive period ofsin[x/|a²−4|] equal8π?
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: The period is 2π|a²−4|; the denominator must be nonzero.
steps: Thus|a²−4|=4, so a²=8 or 0. The values are −2√2,0,2√2, three in all.

problems.title: Reduce shifted trigonometric arguments
problems.question: Simplify sin(π/2+α)tan(π−α)/[cos(3π/2+α)cot(2π−α)].
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: The four factors become cosα,−tanα, sinα,−cotα.
steps: The minus signs cancel. The numerator becomes sinα and the denominatorcosα, so the quotient istanα on the original domain.

problems.title: Difference of two shifted squares
problems.question: Simplify cos²(α−β)−sin²(α+β).
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: Half-angle identities give[cos(2α−2β)+cos(2α+2β)]/2.
steps: The sum-to-product formula reduces this tocos2α·cos2β.

problems.title: A dot product across a dihedral angle
problems.question: PointsA, B lie on different faces of a 120° dihedral. Their feet on the edge are A₁, B₁, with AA₁=1, BB₁=x, A₁B₁=y. FindcosAB₁B.
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: Useedge as the z-axis:A=(1,0,0), B₁=(0,0, y), B=(−x/2,√3x/2, y).
steps: VectorsB₁A=(1,0,−y), B₁B=(−x/2,√3x/2,0) have dot product −x/2.
Their lengths are √(1+y²), x. The cosine is −1/[2√(1+y²)].

problems.title: Pairwise intersecting lines in space
problems.question: Which of statements A, B, C about pairwise intersecting lines are true:nonconcurrent triples force coplanarity; noncoplanar triples force concurrency; the whole family is coplanar or concurrent?
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: Take two intersecting lines with intersection P and their planeΠ. Any line meeting both either passes through P or lies inΠ.
steps: If a third line inΠ avoids P, then any further line through P but outsideΠ cannot meet it. Hence the whole family is coplanar.
Otherwise every line passes through P. This proves C; the extra assumptions in A and B respectively select the coplanar and concurrent alternatives.

problems.title: Maximise area with a fixed diameter
problems.question: A=(cost, sint), B=(−cost,−sint), C=(cos(2−t), sin(2−t)),0<t<1. Whicht maximises are a ABC?
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: AB is a unit-circle diameter of length 2. The triangle are a is|sin(2−2t)|.
steps: The argument2−2t ranges over(0,2), which containsπ/2. The maximum 1 occurs when2−2t=π/2.

problems.title: Two convergent geometric series
problems.question: Forx not a multiple of π/2, letf(x)=cosx+sin²x+cos³x+sin⁴x+… . Findf(2π/3).
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: The odd cosine powers sum tocosx/(1−cos²x); the even sine powers sum tosin²x/(1−sin²x).
steps: Atx=2π/3, the values are cosx=−1/2, sin²x=3/4.

problems.title: A bounded function reaches the quadratic minimiser
problems.question: Find the minimum off(x)²−f(x)+1 for f(x)=|sinx|.
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: The expression is(f(x)−1/2)²+3/4.
steps: Its lower bound3/4 is attained because|sinx|=1/2 is possible.

problems.title: A dihedral relation in two right triangles
problems.question: AKB=AKC=90°, ABK=ACK=α, BAC=γ, and the angle between planes ABC, KBC isβ. Which listed relation holds?
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: AB=AC since AK=ABsinα=ACsinα. LetH be midpoint BC. ThenAH=ABcos(γ/2), and the dihedral angle is AHK=β.
steps: TriangleAKH is right at K, so sinβ=AK/AH=sinα/cos(γ/2).
Rearrange tocos(γ/2)=sinα/sinβ.

problems.title: Combine two right-triangle ratios
problems.question: A projects perpendicularly to O on a second dihedral face and to B on its edge. C is another edge point; ACB=α, ACO=β, and OCB=ABO=δ. Which displayed identity follows?
problems.idea: Apply an exact trigonometric identity or reduce the spatial figure to right triangles.
formulas: Right triangles givecosα/cosβ=BC/CO=cosδ andsinβ/sinα=AO/AB=sinδ.
steps: Square both ratios and add. The result iscos²δ+sin²δ=1.
Thereforecos²α/cos²β+sin²β/sin²α=1.
